chunks: My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: Sa'd bin Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Isa, from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) did not marry any of his wives, nor did he marry off any of his daughters, for more than twelve oqiyah and a nash. The oqiyah is forty dirhams, and the nash is twenty dirhams.

key_terms.أَوْقِيَة: A historical unit of weight or currency, defined here as forty dirhams.
key_terms.دِرْهَم: A silver coin used as a standard unit of currency in Islamic jurisprudence.
key_terms.مَهْر: Dowry or bridal gift given by the husband to the wife in marriage.
key_terms.نَش: A fractional unit of currency or weight, defined here as twenty dirhams.

ai.seo_question: What was the maximum dowry given by the Prophet Muhammad for his wives and daughters?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith to establish a prophetic precedent for modesty in marriage finances, limiting the dowry to twelve oqiyah and a nash (equivalent to 500 dirhams). This specific valuation serves as a key reference in Shia jurisprudence for determining the 'fair dowry' (mahr al-mithl) and discouraging excessive financial burden during the Prophet's era.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Ahmad bin Muhammed bin Isa, from his father, from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, that he said:

The Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, did not marry any of his women, nor did he marry away any of his daughters for more than twelve okes and a nash. An oke is (consisting of) forty dirhams, and a nash is twenty dirhams.
